userStories.title: DB Migrations 042–047 — Search & Marketplace Tables
userStories.description: As the system, I need the database tables for Exa caching, spec research, community publishing, FTS5 search, search provider config, and billing tier expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/db/migrations/042_exa_cache.sql: creates exa_cache table with cache_key (UNIQUE), query, search_type, results_json, created_at, expires_at + indexes on cache_key and expires_at

backend/src/db/migrations/043_spec_research_cache.sql: creates spec_research_cache table with spec_id, workspace_id FK, query, source_url, source_title, excerpt, relevance_score, created_at + index on spec_id
backend/src/db/migrations/044_spec_publications.sql: creates spec_publications table with all fields per spec (FR-124) + indexes on spec_id, exa_indexed, fork_count/download_count
backend/src/db/migrations/045_spec_fts.sql: creates spec_fts FTS5 virtual table with triggers for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on spec_publications
backend/src/db/migrations/046_search_provider_config.sql: creates search_provider_config table, inserts default row (id=1, provider=duckduckgo)
backend/src/db/migrations/047_billing_tier.sql: adds tier, exa_search_enabled, monthly_exa_searches, exa_search_limit columns to billing table using pragma table_info check pattern
All migrations run automatically on server startup without error on a fresh DB
All migrations are idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / pragma checks)
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Exa Search Library — Provider Abstraction
userStories.description: As the execution engine and spec generator, I need a search provider abstraction that auto-selects Exa, SearXNG, or DuckDuckGo based on configuration and falls back gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/exa-search.ts created with: search(), searchExa(), searchSearxng(), searchDuckDuckGo(), getCachedResults(), setCachedResults(), purgeExpiredCache() functions
search() reads RORCA_SEARCH_PROVIDER env var (exa | searxng | duckduckgo), defaults to duckduckgo
searchExa() uses exa-js SDK, type: 'neural' default, numResults: 5 default
getCachedResults() queries exa_cache table by SHA256(query + search_type) cache key
setCachedResults() writes to exa_cache with expires_at = now + 24 hours
Exa timeout > 5000ms falls back to searchDuckDuckGo(), response includes provider: 'duckduckgo', fallback: true
Exponential backoff on Exa failure: 1s, 2s, 4s delays, max 3 retries before fallback
purgeExpiredCache() deletes rows WHERE expires_at < datetime('now'), called on server startup and daily at 03:00 via scheduler
EXA_API_KEY env var used, vault key (key_name='exa') takes precedence over env var
SearchResult interface: { results: ExaResult[], provider: string, cached: boolean, latencyMs: number }
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Spec Generation Research Pre-Pass
userStories.description: As a spec author, I want Rorca to research best practices via Exa before writing stories so the generated spec references real library APIs instead of hallucinated ones.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate checks if RORCA_SEARCH_PROVIDER=exa before running pre-pass
Pre-pass: extracts technology names from brief using simple pattern matching (look for known tech keywords: React, Next.js, Stripe, Prisma, Tailwind, etc.)
For each detected technology, queries Exa: 'best practices [technology] [feature]' where feature is inferred from brief
Top 3 results per technology injected as context block into spec generation prompt before story writing

Context block format: '## Research Sources
[title]: [excerpt]
URL: [url]
...'
Pre-pass results stored in spec_research_cache linked to generated spec_id
If Exa fails or times out, spec generation continues without research (graceful degradation)
Pre-pass adds no more than 2000 tokens to spec generation prompt (enforced by truncation)
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Spec Sanitizer — PII Scrubbing
userStories.description: As the system, I need a sanitizer that removes PII and secrets from spec JSON before it can be published to the community marketplace.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/spec-sanitizer.ts created with sanitizeSpec(specJson, workspacePath) function
Scrubs: OpenAI keys (sk-...), Anthropic keys (sk-ant-...), GitHub tokens (ghp_...), URLs with credentials, email addresses, macOS/Linux/Windows home paths
Replaces all matched patterns with [REDACTED]
Replaces all occurrences of workspacePath with [WORKSPACE_PATH]
Preserves all story content: title, description, acceptanceCriteria, tags, model, dependsOn
Returns sanitized object (does not mutate input)
Unit test: sanitizeSpec with a spec containing a fake sk-ant-key123... → key replaced with [REDACTED]
Unit test: sanitizeSpec with workspace path in description → replaced with [WORKSPACE_PATH]
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Community Marketplace — Publish & Fork Routes
userStories.description: As a user, I want to publish my completed specs to the community and fork others' specs into my workspace.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/routes/marketplace.ts created with @swagger annotations

DELETE /api/marketplace/:id: removes publication (only by original publisher workspace)
GET /api/marketplace/popular: returns top 20 by fork_count + download_count, with pagination

userStories.title: Community Marketplace — Search (FTS5 + Exa)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to search the community spec marketplace to find specs that match what I'm trying to build.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/marketplace/search?q=<query>&tags=<csv>&minPassRate=<0-1>&minStoryCount=<n>&maxStoryCount=<n>&page=<n>&limit=<n>
When RORCA_SEARCH_PROVIDER=duckduckgo or searxng: uses SQLite FTS5 query: SELECT * FROM spec_fts WHERE spec_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY rank
When RORCA_SEARCH_PROVIDER=exa: queries exa_search lib, maps results back to spec_publications rows by URL/title matching
Filters applied after search: tags (JSON array contains), pass_rate >= minPassRate, story_count BETWEEN minStoryCount AND maxStoryCount
Returns: { items: Publication[], total: number, page: number, pageSize: number }
Each Publication includes: id, title, description, tags, storyCount, passRate, model, publisherHandle (null if anonymous), forkCount, downloadCount, createdAt
Empty query (q='') returns popular specs (sorted by fork_count DESC)
Search latency < 500ms for FTS5 on 10,000 publications
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Telemetry Opt-In & Privacy
userStories.description: As a self-hosted user, I want to know that no data leaves my machine by default so I can trust Rorca with my codebase.
acceptanceCriteria: RORCA_TELEMETRY env var: default unset (= disabled). Must be explicitly set to '1' to enable

On first startup (onboarding_state has no 'telemetry_asked' entry), show a one-time banner: 'Help improve Rorca by sharing anonymous usage stats. No code or spec content is ever sent.' with 'Enable' and 'No thanks' buttons
Enable sets RORCA_TELEMETRY=1 in backend/.env (appends), marks onboarding_state telemetry_asked=true
No thanks marks onboarding_state telemetry_asked=true, does nothing else
When telemetry disabled: no outbound HTTP calls except to configured LLM providers and Exa (if configured by user)
GET /api/health includes telemetryEnabled: boolean
Settings panel shows telemetry toggle with current state + description of what is/isn't collected
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes
